study_context.treatment: Intensive blood pressure control (systolic BP target <120 mmHg)
study_context.population: Non-diabetic adults aged ≥50 with hypertension and increased cardiovascular risk

Adults aged 65\u201374 derive meaningful.hypothesis: Adults aged 65–74 derive meaningful cardiovascular benefit from intensive BP lowering because they have elevated baseline risk but still relatively low frailty.

In participants with baseline systolic b.hypothesis: In participants with baseline systolic blood pressure <130 mmHg, intensive BP control (target <120 mmHg) will offer little to no benefit on the composite cardiovascular outcome compared with standard control.

subgroup_rule.description: Baseline systolic blood pressure less than 130 mmHg

In participants with baseline diastolic.hypothesis: In participants with baseline diastolic blood pressure <70 mmHg, intensive systolic BP control (target <120 mmHg) is associated with worse composite cardiovascular outcomes compared with standard control.

subgroup_rule.description: Baseline diastolic blood pressure less than 70 mmHg

Among adults with eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73.hypothesis: Among adults with eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2, intensive systolic BP control (target <120 mmHg) will provide less reduction in the composite of major cardiovascular events compared with standard BP management.

subgroup_rule.description: Participants with estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (indicating chronic kidney disease stage 3 or worse).
